bihar_raw_news.content: UP, Bihar in rain zone as Delhi moves past days of heavy showers Bihar, already reeling from widespread flooding and swollen rivers, could see little respite from the wet conditions. By CNBCTV18.com September 8, 2026, 5:00:56 AM IST (Published) The rain spell is likely to ease over Delhi and parts of northwest India on Tuesday, September 8, even as Bihar, West Bengal and parts of Uttar Pradesh remain under pressure from heavy rainfall. A low-pressure area over central Uttar Pradesh is driving the weather over north and east India. The India Meteorological Department has forecast fairly widespread to widespread rain over Bihar through September 9, with isolated heavy rainfall likely from September 8-10. Bihar, already reeling from widespread flooding and swollen rivers, could see little respite from the wet conditions. The state recorded 12 cm of rain at Laukahi in Madhubani in the 24 hours ending 8.30 am on Monday. The IMD has also warned of thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds in Bihar through the week. In West Bengal and Sikkim, the weather is likely to remain active, with fairly widespread to widespread rain over Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim through September 13. Gangetic West Bengal is also likely to see widespread rain through September 10, with heavy rainfall possible through September 9. East Uttar Pradesh is another area to watch on Tuesday, with isolated heavy rainfall forecast. West Uttar Pradesh could also see isolated rain, while rainfall activity over Uttarakhand is expected to be more scattered. For Delhi, the recent spell of heavy rain is set to ease significantly. The capital is forecast to see a partly cloudy sky with no warning on Tuesday, with temperatures expected to range between 25°C and 34°C. The IMD expects similar conditions over the next few days. Central India will continue to see scattered showers and thunderstorms, particularly over Madhya Pradesh and Vidarbha, while Konkan and Goa are likely to receive fairly widespread to widespread rainfall through September 13. Across the south, rainfall is expected to remain relatively subdued, with isolated to scattered showers over several states. Telangana could see gusty winds through September 9, while Kerala is likely to remain hot and humid throughout the day. Continue Reading Tags IMD forecast

bihar_raw_news.title: Tejashwi Yadav urges Centre to declare Bihar floods a national disaster
bihar_raw_news.content: Tejashwi Yadav urges Centre to declare Bihar floods a national disaster RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav has urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to declare Bihar’s floods a national disaster and provide Rs 5,000 crore in immediate assistance. He also sought enhanced rescue operations, farmer relief, an audit and a long-term flood resilience mission By IANS Published Date - 8 September 2026, 12:15 AM Patna: As severe floods continue to affect large parts of Bihar, Leader of the Opposition Tejashwi Yadav has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, urging the Centre to declare the situation a national disaster and provide immediate financial assistance of Rs 5,000 crore to the state. More than a dozen districts have been affected by the floods, with lakhs of people facing difficulties caused by rising river levels, damaged infrastructure and disrupted connectivity. In his letter, Yadav said the situation had affected 20 districts and caused extensive damage to life, property and public infrastructure. He said flood-affected people were struggling to access basic necessities, including food, clean drinking water, medicines, electricity, cattle fodder and safe transportation. Yadav criticised the relief and rescue measures being undertaken by the Bihar government and the NDA-led Centre, describing the assistance as inadequate considering the scale of the crisis. He also accused the Bihar government and NDA leaders from the state of failing to secure adequate central assistance and a national-disaster declaration. The RJD leader argued that Bihar’s recurring floods are not solely a natural disaster but also reflect years of inadequate disaster preparedness, mitigation and adaptation. He pointed out that despite floods occurring almost every year, sufficient measures for a permanent solution have not been implemented. Yadav also raised questions over the state government’s financial preparedness for the crisis. He alleged that Bihar’s Contingency Fund and other financial resources had been diverted towards routine government expenditure, leaving insufficient funds for flood relief. The RJD leader called for an independent review or CAG audit of the state’s financial and disaster-management preparedness and the utilisation of the State Contingency Fund. In his letter, Yadav urged the Prime Minister and the Central Government to take immediate measures, including declare the devastating floods in Bihar a national disaster, provide Rs 5,000 crore in immediate financial assistance along with a special flood-relief package, deploy additional boats and other resources to flood-hit areas where road connectivity has been disrupted, deploy the Army and Air Force wherever necessary for rescue and relief operations and ensure assistance through helicopters, ensure adequate supplies of food, drinking water, medicines, animal fodder and temporary shelters, provide special financial assistance to farmers, labourers, livestock owners and affected families, and conduct an independent review or CAG audit of the state’s disaster-management preparedness and the utilisation and transactions of the State Contingency Fund. Yadav also called for a comprehensive, long-term Flood Resilience Mission to address Bihar’s recurring flood crisis. According to him, the mission should focus on river and embankment management, drainage systems, rejuvenation of water bodies, modern flood forecasting and improved water-management policies. national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah today chaired the 28th meeting of the Western Zonal Council at Panaji in Goa. Addressing the gathering, Mr Shah said, there are no longer any disputes among the states of the Western Region, which is a major achievement. He emphasized that the Zonal Councils have evolved from forums for dispute resolution into platforms for monitoring the implementation of public welfare schemes. Mr Shah said that all the issues discussed in today’s meeting were related to monitoring. He noted that several disputes between States over rivers have also been resolved in the Zonal Council. Shah said the councils are also monitoring key welfare indicators, including child malnutrition, underweight and stunting, along with Aadhaar coverage and the implementation of Ayushman Bharat cards. Mr Shah said, over the last 12 years, Prime Minister Modi has strengthened cooperative federalism, with Zonal Council meetings increasing nearly threefold since 2014. He said, during 2004 to 2014, the total number of meetings of the Zonal Councils and their Standing Committees was only 25, whereas since 2014, a total of 71 meetings of the Zonal Councils and their Standing Committees have been held. He said 1,445 of a total of 1,893 issues discussed in these meetings have been resolved, reflecting the effectiveness of the councils and the spirit of Team India. Noting that the Western region is extremely important from several perspectives, the Home Minister said this region is the country’s largest economic, industrial and financial centre. He said, Goa contributes much more to economic growth than its geographical size would suggest due to advanced tourism, high per capita income and mines. He pointed out that since 2014, Prime Minister Modi has continuously worked, along with numerous administrative reforms, to transform the country’s economy into a rapidly moving economy. He said that Daman and Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and the three states of the Western Zonal Council have also made a significant contribution towards achieving the growth rate of 7.8 per cent. Mr Shah said, the Western Region is known as the WEST Engine of the country’s economic growth. W stands for wealth and finance, which are generated in this region; E stands for exports and ports; S stands for start-ups and semiconductors; and T stands for tourism and the blue economy, in which the Western Region has the largest share in the country. The Home Minister said, recently, the country recorded a growth rate of 7.8 per cent in the first quarter of the financial year 2026-2027. Mr Shah further mentioned that the Indian economy recording such a growth rate amid global turbulence is a matter of pride . At the 28th meeting of the Western Zonal Council, several extremely important issues were discussed for the member states as well as for the country. These included the implementation of Fast Track Special Courts for speedy investigation and early disposal of cases of rape against women and children, issues related to the Emergency Response Support System (ERSS-112), issues related to food safety standards, Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana, provision of brick-and-mortar banking facilities within the prescribed radius of every village, issues related to railway development projects, issues concerning environmental clearances, and others. In addition, issues of national importance were also discussed, including urban master planning, issues related to electricity supply, strengthening Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACSs), eliminating malnutrition among children through the Poshan Abhiyaan, reducing the school dropout rate among school children, participation of public hospitals in the Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana, and issues related to cybercrime and digital infrastructure, among others. The meeting was attended by Goa Chief Minister Pramod Sawant, Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, and Administrator of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu Praful K Patel. Senior officials of the Central government and the state governments, as well as the Union Territory, also participated in the meeting of the council.

national_raw_news.title: Arunachal media delegation explores Gujarat's development journey, heritage and infrastructure
national_raw_news.content: Echo Of Arunachal Newsflash State News Arunachal media delegation explores Gujarat’s development journey, heritage and infrastructure Ahmedabad, Sep 7: A nine-member media delegation from Arunachal Pradesh began its seven-day press tour of Gujarat on Monday, visiting key institutions and projects showcasing the State’s development in governance, urban planning, heritage and transport infrastructure. The tour commenced at the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Ahmedabad, where the delegation was welcomed by Additional Director General Siddhartha Bodke. Interacting with the visiting journalists, Bodke briefed them on PIB’s role in disseminating information on government policies, programmes and initiatives and encouraged the media team to make the most of the field visits and expert interactions lined up during the tour. The delegation next visited Kochrab Ashram, Mahatma Gandhi's first ashram established after returning from South Africa in 1915, where the journalists interacted with Dr Prasana Gandhi, who briefed them on the historical and cultural significance of the Ashram and its association with the Father of the Nation, his philosophy and India’s freedom movement. The journalists also undertook a cruise on the Sabarmati River, observing the riverfront development and the surrounding urban landscape. The visit provided an opportunity to understand Ahmedabad’s riverfront transformation and its integration with the city’s urban development. At Centre for Environmental Planning and Technology (CEPT) University, the delegation interacted with President Barjor Mehta and senior faculty members on architecture, urban planning, education and research. The interaction also covered the institution’s contribution to shaping urban environments through education and research. The first day concluded with a visit to the Sabarmati Multimodal Transport Hub, where the delegation was briefed on the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail (MAHSR) project. The interaction covered the scale and technical complexity of India’s first high-speed rail corridor, including engineering, planning, inter-agency coordination and on-ground execution. During the visit, Joint Director, PIB Itanagar, Utsav Parmar, also called on Principal Chief Project Manager Rajesh Agarwal. The seven-day press tour will take the Arunachal media delegation to several key sites and institutions across Gujarat, covering infrastructure, industry, technology, education, heritage and culture. The tour is aimed at providing the journalists with direct field exposure to major development initiatives and projects shaping Gujarat, enabling them to gain a broader understanding of the State’s development experience and its relevance to the diverse development landscape of the country. national_raw_news.title: US: MoS Jitin Prasada participates in G20 Innovation Ministers' meeting in Chapel Hill
national_raw_news.content: US: MoS Jitin Prasada participates in G20 Innovation Ministers’ meeting in Chapel Hill Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर US: MoS Jitin Prasada participates in G20 Innovation Ministers’ meeting in Chapel Hill ANI | Updated: Sep 07, 2026 22:00 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel North Carolina [US], September 7 (ANI): The Union Minister of State (MoS) Jitin Prasada led the Indian delegation at the G20 Innovation Ministers’ meeting held on September 1 and September 2 in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, United States (US), hosted by the US Department of Commerce and the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP). According to the Ministry of Electronics and IT, the MoS was accompanied by Ajit Kumar, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), senior officials from MeitY, Department of Science and Technology (DST) and Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), as well as officials of the Embassy of India in the US. At the conclusion of the Ministerial, the G20 Ministers released the Innovation Ministerial Statement recognising that “emerging technologies have the potential to unlock prosperity, enhance productivity, and expand opportunity for all our peoples.” The consensus statement articulates shared broad agreement across six pillars, pro-innovation policy frameworks, technology for opportunity and prosperity, skilled technical workforce development, intellectual property policies for artificial intelligence (AI), AI for standards and standards for AI, and industrial innovation and investment in supply chains. Ministers also reached consensus on the Carolina Principles for Emerging Technologies, which call on countries to invest in foundational research, strengthen commercialisation pathways, and enable trusted technology adoption and deployment. Other deliverables of the Ministerial included the AI Prosperity Objectives and the AI Prosperity Compact, which will further technical workforce development across G20 nations and expand opportunities for private sector partnership. On the sidelines of the G20 Ministerial, Prasada held several bilateral discussions. In his bilateral meeting with Henna Virkkunen, Executive Vice-President of the European Commission, both discussed the importance of strengthening cooperation in innovation and building trusted digital ecosystems that enable technology-led growth and shared prosperity. In the meeting with Anne Le Hénanff, Minister Delegate for Artificial Intelligence and Digital Affairs of France, both sides discussed advancing cooperation in AI and digital technologies. India and France remain committed to strengthening technology-driven innovation and building partnerships for a trusted digital future, the Ministry said. During the meeting with Thomas Jarzombek and Silke Launert, Parliamentary State Secretaries, Germany, MoS explored opportunities to further deepen India–Germany collaboration in technology, innovation and research, driving shared progress and future-ready partnerships. In discussions with Prof Gaspard Banyankimbona, Commissioner for Education, Science, Technology and Innovation, African Union, the commitment to deepening partnership with Africa and creating new opportunities for shared growth and prosperity was highlighted by offering India Stack digital solutions, including DPI, to African countries. In the bilateral discussion with Howard Lutnick, US Secretary of Commerce, both sides exchanged views on strengthening cooperation across Semiconductors, AI and Data Centres. national_raw_news.title: Media Delegation from Kerala begins Seven-Day Press Tour to JK - Kashmir Convener
national_raw_news.content: Media Delegation from Kerala begins Seven-Day Press Tour to JK - Kashmir Convener J&K Media Delegation from Kerala begins Seven-Day Press Tour to JK By Desk Editor Published on Sep 7, 2026 Share Convener News Desk Srinagar, September 7: A 13-member media delegation from Kerala has embarked on a seven-day press tour to Jammu and Kashmir from September 6 to 12, 2026. The tour is being organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Kochi, with the objective of providing journalists from Kerala an opportunity to gain first-hand insights into the developmental initiatives, infrastructure projects and achievements in the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir. On the first day of the tour, the delegation visited the Press Information Bureau office in Srinagar. Shri Qazi Salman, Director, PIB Srinagar, welcomed the members of the delegation and provided an overview of the media and communication landscape in Kashmir. He also interacted with the visiting journalists and shared insights into the functioning of PIB in the region. Later in the day, the delegation visited Gulmarg, the picturesque hill station located in Baramulla district of Jammu and Kashmir, and experienced the region’s rich natural landscape and scenic beauty. During the week long tour, the media delegation will visit various developmental projects and important locations across the Union Territory. The press tour aims to familiarise the participating journalists with the developmental transformation taking place in Jammu and Kashmir and provide them an opportunity to interact with the stakeholders. The press tour is part of PIB’s efforts to facilitate wider awareness and informed reporting on significant developmental initiatives being undertaken across different regions of the country. national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Finance Union Finance Minister meets delegation of bank employees representing different Public Sector Banks (PSBs) Scheme of Performance Linked Incentives (PLI) to Executives of Public Sector Banks kept in abeyance in response to Employees’ concerns Posted On: 07 SEP 2026 9:05PM by PIB Delhi The Union Finance Minister today met with a delegation of bank employees representing different Public Sector Banks (PSBs) led by the Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh. The delegation raised various issues relating to the banking sector including review of ex-gratia, medical facility for retired employees, revisiting the present structure of Performance Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme applicable for the employees of PSBs, and other concerns related to employees. The concerns expressed by bank employees were taken cognizance of, and in response to the representation received on the PLI structure, it was decided to keep in abeyance the implementation of the PLI Scheme dated 19.11.2024 for FY 2025–26 and take up the same during the ongoing Bipartite Settlement/ Joint Note discussions. The Government is committed to resolve issues through dialogue, consultation and mutual understanding in the larger interest of bank employees, customers and the banking sector. **** SR/AD (Release ID: 2307672) Visitor Counter : 3241 Read this release in: Marathi Ministry of Finance Union Finance Minister meets delegation of bank employees representing different Public Sector Banks (PSBs) Scheme of Performance Linked Incentives (PLI) to Executives of Public Sector Banks kept in abeyance in response to Employees’ concerns Posted On: 07 SEP 2026 9:05PM by PIB Delhi The Union Finance Minister today met with a delegation of bank employees representing different Public Sector Banks (PSBs) led by the Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh.
